_note: Kalman parameter file derived from parameters/xiong-2018.json and from the
noise settings of the Simulink model that produced out.mat.
PID: only the first-order terms are kept, Kp = a1, Kd = a2, Ki = a3;
the high-order integral terms a4, a5, b1, b2 are dropped by decision of the
mems_out is a fixed point code of the PID output: u[V] = code * 7 / 65536,
which is applied by units.u below so the estimator sees volts.
Phase 2 FOH variant: same device, noise, data, units and evaluation
windows as the ZOH file of the same name. The acceleration prior is
the six state first order hold model of the V2.1 task sheet.

_derivation.K_s: k_cv * k_adc = 4 * v_ref * C0 / (Cf * gap) * 1 = 4.7825831127e7 V/m
_derivation.K_p: a1 of the state space PID
_derivation.K_i: a3 of the state space PID, because inter0[k] = inter0[k-1] + e[k-1]
_derivation.K_d: a2 of the state space PID, because diff = e[k] - e[k-1]
_derivation.u_code_scale: mems_out = round(pid_V * 65536/7), verified with zero residual on 1001 samples; LSB = 1.068115e-4 V
_derivation.sigma_n2: Band-Limited White Noise at the C/V output: noise power 9.313e-15 V^2/Hz, sample time 1/fs, so sigma_n^2 = 9.313e-15 * 128000 = 1.192064e-9 V^2 (sigma_n = 3.4526e-5 V)
_derivation.mechanical_noise_psd: Brownian noise into the spring damper: noise power 5e-17 g^2/Hz, sample time 1/fs/1000; one sided ASD = sqrt(2*5e-17) g/sqrt(Hz) = 10 ng/sqrt(Hz); as a two sided PSD in SI = 5e-17 * 9.81^2 = 4.811805e-15 (m/s^2)^2/Hz
notes: The electrostatic force is averaged over one sampling period by the impulse
theorem: F = duty_cycle * F_feedback.  The bias force of the detection phase
is not part of the model, so k stays at its bare value 859.1382065499873 N/m.
No negative stiffness term is introduced.
Observability of the closed loop pair (F, H): the scaled observability matrix
has rank 5, condition number about 2.1e4 and no undetectable mode, so all five
states including the external acceleration are observable.
The steady state PID output of the 9.81 m/s^2 step is 1.864716 V after the code
conversion, and a*m/|K_u| gives 1.864721 V, a relative difference of 3e-6.
That cross checks K_u, m and the code scale against an independent path.
The data was produced with the first-order PID terms only, as confirmed by the
task owner.  Running the same three term model from rest over the 1001 samples
reproduces the measured step response to 1.1e-5 in steady state, and the
settled PID noise is 2.32e-3 V measured against 1.82e-3 V modelled (ratio 0.79)
with no DC bias (-2.3e-6 V).  The 21 percent shortfall in noise gain is

_derivation.prior_model: FOH: X = [x, v, a, j, I, h]; A of section 18; q_j is the per sample variance of the Jerk boundary increment.
_derivation.P0_FOH: Assembled from the phase 1 5x5 P0 with the selection matrix of section 15.1: S P0 S^T puts the five common states in rows/columns 1,2,3,5,6; jerk_var0 = 0 because the initial Jerk is known to be zero (jerk_init_mode = known). No arbitrary number is inserted.
_derivation.q_j: manual entry 0.001 (m/s^3)^2, set by hand after the manual trial recorded in the phase 2 report; no automatic scan is implemented. It is not q_a and the numeric equality would carry no meaning.

zoh_reference.note: Relative tolerance of the compatibility regression; the record was captured before the FOH upgrade and is checked by `main.py reference` and tests/test_regression_zoh.py.
